title: Alternating Magnetic Field-Responsive Hybrid Gelatin Microgels for Controlled Drug Release
protocol: Prepare a crosslinker genipin solution by dissolving 20 mg of genipin in 2 ml of phosphate buffered saline (1x PBS; pH 7.4).
Vortex the genipin solution and place it in a 50 °C water bath for 2 hours to dissolve completely.

Prepare a surfactant solution by dissolving 20 mg of poly(ethylene glycol)-poly(propylene glycol)-poly(ethylene glycol) (Mw = 2,900 Da; referred to as L64) in 200 ml of PBS at the concentration of 100 ppm.
Prepare a 15% (w/v) gelatin solution by dissolving 64.5 mg of gelatin in 0.43 ml of PBS.
Vortex the gelatin solution and place it on a water bath at 37 °C until it reaches a sol phase, where the solution becomes fluidic.
Vortex the gelatin solution 2 - 3 times to ensure homogeneity of the sample.
Disperse 10.75 mg of hydrophilic MNPs in 0.43 ml of PBS.
Dissolve 12.9 mg of p(NIPAM-co-AAm) in the MNP suspension to make a concentration at 3% (w/v).
Dissolve 0.5 mg of Texas-Red conjugated bovine serum albumin (TR-BSA; Mw ~66 kDa) in the mixture of p(NIPAM-co-AAm)/MNPs.

Prepare mixtures of gelatin/p(NIPAM-co-AAm)/MNPs/BSA solution by adding 0.43 ml of p(NIPAM-co-AAm)/MNPs mixture into 0.43 ml of gelatin solution and thoroughly vortexing to create a homogeneous mixture.
Pour 15 ml of silicone oil (polydimethylsiloxane, viscosity 350 cSt) into a clean and sterile beaker.
Add the pre-prepared aqueous mixtures of gelatin/p(NIPAM-co-AAm)/MNPs/BSA solution (0.86 ml) to the silicone oil.
Emulsify the aqueous mixture in the oil phase by stirring with a magnetic stirring bar at 900 rpm at 30 °C for 30 min.
Transfer the emulsion (~16 ml) from the beaker into a 50 ml tube.
Cool down the tube for 10 min at 4 °C to allow gelation of the micro-droplets in the oil.
Fill the tube with prepared L64 solution (at  4 °C) up to 50 ml and vigorously shake the tube.
Centrifuge the tube for 20 min at 2,300 x g at 4 °C.
Regularly check for the presence of a pellet of gel particles on the side of the tube.
If no pellet is seen after centrifuging, repeat the centrifugation process for another 20 min at the same speed and temperature.
Carefully remove supernatant without disturbing the pellet formed on the inner wall of the tube.
Add 2 ml of genipin solution to the pellet of gel particles and mix well by vortexing.
Transfer the tube containing the suspension into a water bath at 23°C for crosslinking reaction.
Discard the genipin solution after crosslinking.
Resuspend the microgels in PBS and centrifuge at 2,300 x g (4°C) for 20 min.
Break apart formed pellet with a pipette tip if necessary.
Wash the microgels by repeating the resuspension and centrifugation steps up to three times as needed.
Discard the supernatant after washing.
Resuspend the microgels in PBS at a desired density using a hemocytometer count.
Load the microgel suspension between a slide glass and cover slip for microscopic observation.
Seal the boundary of the cover slip with epoxy resin.
Place the tube with desired concentration of microgels in aqueous media into the chamber of magnetic coils.
Insert a fiber optic temperature probe into the tube if necessary to monitor temperature change during AMF application.
Apply high frequency (>100 kHz) AMF at a defined field strength (>5 kA/m) for a specified duration.
Centrifuge the sample tube for 20 min at 2,273 x g (4°C).
Collect the supernatant to quantify the amount of TR-BSA released from microgel using spectrophotometry.
Use excitation and emission wavelengths of 584 nm and 612 nm, respectively, for Texas Red.
